title: Wave Properties
seo_title: Wave Worksheets: v = fλ, Frequency, Wavelength and the EM Spectrum (High School Physics)
standard_text: Use mathematical representations to support a claim regarding relationships among the frequency, wavelength, and speed of waves traveling in various media.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on wave properties (NGSS HS-PS4-1): v = fλ, period, waves in different media, sound and light, and the electromagnetic spectrum. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The medium sets the speed; in a new medium the wavelength changes but the frequency stays.
body_html:
How to think about it

Wave speed = frequency × wavelength (v = fλ).

  • The medium sets the speed. In one medium, higher frequency means shorter wavelength.
  • When a wave enters a new medium, its speed and wavelength change, but its frequency stays the same.
  • Period T = 1 ÷ f. All electromagnetic waves travel at 3.0 × 108 m/s in a vacuum.
Example

Sound: 343 m/s, 686 Hz. λ?

343 ÷ 686

Answer: 0.5 m

Example

Frequency 4 Hz. Period?

1 ÷ 4

Answer: 0.25 s

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a higher frequency makes a wave faster in the same medium.
  • Thinking frequency changes when a wave enters a new medium.
  • Writing v = f ÷ λ.

faq.q: How are wave speed, frequency and wavelength related?
faq.a: v = fλ. If the speed stays the same, a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength.

faq.q: What changes when a wave enters a new medium?
faq.a: Its speed and wavelength change. Its frequency stays the same because it is set by the source.

faq.q: How fast do electromagnetic waves travel?
faq.a: All electromagnetic waves travel at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
